i0-context.title: Load baseline context
i0-context.imperative: Load issue #688 (grip-fit rain exclusion too aggressive), its related issues (#678 spike comment, #687, #663, #664), the glossary, and the grip/weather code and map packets. Record pass when loaded.
i0-context.finding: Loaded: issue #688 body; #678 (identifiability) + its two owner comments incl. the 2026-07-25 G-pooling spike writeup naming #688 as coverage item 5; #687 (sibling fit-quality hole); #664 (consumer, closed); grip_baseline.py, grip_batch.py, grip_store.py; src/data/weather_features.py; src/physics/burn_rate_calibration.py; schema.sql; packets physics.md + data.md.

q1.title: Where does the 'rain exclusion' that dropped 20 of 36 weekends actually live -- production grip code, or the spike?
q1.imperative: Read src/physics/layer2/grip_baseline.py and grip_batch.py end to end and determine whether any production path DROPS a rain-flagged session, or whether rain only widens sigma. Record the code evidence.
q1.finding: FACT RESOLVED -- no production grip path drops a rain session. run_grip_batch (grip_batch.py:66-95) walks every calendar GP x session_type and upserts whatever fit_session_grip_baseline returns; the ONLY skip is the store.has() idempotency guard. rain_flag is consumed at exactly two places, grip_baseline.py:481-482 and :548-549, and both only MULTIPLY session_offset_sigma by RAIN_SIGMA_INFLATION=4.0. The 20-of-36 weekend drop therefore happened in the #678 spike's own candidate-weekend selection (scratchpad/g-pool-spike/proto{1,2}/, never committed; the only committed spike is proto/x2 at 8ce31394, a different one). The issue's premise is misattributed to grip_baseline: the defect is that no production selection predicate exists, so each consumer invents its own -- and the only universally-available signal to invent it from is the any-wet-sample bool.

q2.title: [fact] What wet signals exist in the canonical DB, and what is each one's real coverage?
q2.imperative: Enumerate every stored wet signal (sessions.rainfall blob, weather.rainfall per-sample, session_surface_features.session_rain_flag / wet_lap_count / wet_lap_fraction, lap_times.compound) and MEASURE coverage per season and session_type. Record evidence.
q2.finding: FACT RESOLVED -- four wet signals, wildly different coverage (probe_coverage.py + probe_rain.py, this work area). (a) sessions.rainfall: an int64 blob = count of wet weather SAMPLES; present every year; the only universally-available signal, and the one rain_flag_from_raw reads. (b) weather.rainfall per-sample rows: present 2022/2023, ABSENT for many 2024 sessions (2024 Australia/Q, Canada/Q, Canada/R, Spain/R, Austria/R, GreatBritain/Q, GreatBritain/R all have 0 weather rows despite a nonzero sessions.rainfall count) -- so a fraction-of-weather-samples rule silently reads 0/0 there. (c) session_surface_features.session_rain_flag: populated 2022/2023 only; ZERO rows 2024/2025. (d) session_surface_features.wet_lap_fraction: populated for session_type='R' ONLY -- 22/22, 22/22, 24/24, 24/24 races across 2022-2025 and ZERO non-race sessions in any season. (e) lap_times.compound: universally present; it is the substrate (d) is computed from.

q3.title: [fact] Does this repo already have a precedented graded wet-exclusion seam?
q3.imperative: Search for an existing named wet threshold plus stored-fraction read in physics. Record the seam, its threshold constant, and whether the architecture map sanctions the physics-to-data read.
q3.finding: FACT RESOLVED -- yes, and it is map-sanctioned. src/physics/burn_rate_calibration.py:698 defines WET_EXCLUDE_THRESHOLD = 0.05 ('wet-lap fraction above which a race is treated as rain-affected and excluded from the dry-race fuel-burn baseline'), and :709 session_wet_fraction(year, gp, db_path) READS the stored session_surface_features.wet_lap_fraction rather than recomputing compounds. docs/architecture/packets/physics.md:143-147 and :161 document exactly this physics-consumes-stored-wet-flag arrangement, and :2833 names it an allowed physics->data read. Producer side: src/data/weather_features.session_wet_lap_features / populate_wet_features_for_db, CLI scripts/populate_wet_features.py, mapped at packets/data.md:88-93. So issue #688 does not need a new instrument -- it needs the existing one extended to the sessions the grip fit runs over.

q4.title: [fact] On real 2022-2024 data, does the issue's proposed fraction-of-wet-SAMPLES threshold actually discriminate a brief shower from genuinely wet running?
q4.imperative: Compute per timed session the wet-weather-sample fraction and the WET/INTERMEDIATE lap fraction; look for sessions where the two disagree. Record counterexamples.
q4.finding: FACT RESOLVED -- NO. On real 2022-2024 timed sessions the wet-SAMPLE fraction fails in BOTH directions vs the WET/INTERMEDIATE lap fraction (probe_rain.py). FALSE KEEP: 2023 Belgium Q has 1 wet sample of 95 (sample-fraction 0.011, under every candidate threshold) but 212 of 341 laps on wet tyres (lap-fraction 0.622) -- a sample-fraction rule KEEPS a soaked qualifying session. FALSE DROP: 2022 Hungary R has 46 wet samples of 167 (0.275, above every candidate threshold) but ZERO wet laps -- a dry race; same shape at 2022 Miami R (0.056/0.000), 2022 GreatBritain R (0.044/0.000), 2023 Austria R (0.020/0.000), and 2024 Hungary Q (0.762/0.000 -- 76% of samples wet, not one wet lap). Conclusion: acceptance option A as literally written ('a fraction-of-wet-samples threshold') is the measurably WRONG instrument; acceptance option B ('materially wet during the timed running') is the right one, and the lap-compound fraction is its operational form.

q5.title: [fact] Does the grip fit ingest wet laps at all -- what is actually at risk from a wet session?
q5.imperative: Read _read_clean_session_laps compound filter and _wear_corrected_pace. Determine whether the risk is wet laps entering the fit, or dry laps sitting on a DRYING track.
q5.finding: FACT RESOLVED -- the fit never ingests a wet lap. _read_clean_session_laps hard-filters compound IN ('SOFT','MEDIUM','HARD') (grip_baseline.py:215), matching tyre_supplant.DRY_COMPOUNDS. So the exposure is NOT wet laps polluting the curve. It is two other things: (i) a mixed session's SURVIVING DRY laps sit on a DRYING track, whose falling lap times are drying, not rubber accumulation -- a direct violation of the monotone-rubber-in model _saturating() encodes, and the one hazard the issue's own 'monotone-grip assumption still needs dry' caveat is pointing at; (ii) a mixed session may retain too few dry stints, which MIN_STINTS_FOR_FIT=2 plus the thin_fallback path already handles honestly. This means a pure severity threshold is necessary but NOT sufficient -- a residual drying-track guard belongs in the plan.

q6.title: [DECISION] Which severity criterion do we adopt: weather-sample fraction, WET/INTERMEDIATE lap fraction, or a composite with an explicit unknown state?
q6.imperative: Recommend, then take to the counterpart. Never self-answer without recorded authority.
q6.finding: DECISION RULED (self-adjudicated under the dispatching human's standing directive; see human_answer) -- adopt the stored WET/INTERMEDIATE LAP fraction as the primary criterion, expressed as an explicit graded severity with an UNKNOWN state, never a bare bool: dry | mixed | wet | unknown. The weather-sample count survives only as a fallback when the lap signal is missing, and coverage-absent resolves to 'unknown' (widened, never silently 'dry'). Grounds: q4 shows the sample-fraction instrument is wrong in both directions on real data; q3 shows the lap-fraction instrument is already precedented and map-sanctioned in this repo's fuel subsystem; q2 shows the sample source has real 2024 coverage holes that would read as 0/0.

q7.title: [DECISION] Does the fix REPLACE the binary rain_flag, or add a graded field alongside it (record and stored-DB compatibility)?
q7.imperative: Weigh the GripEstimateRecord additive-migration contract and every existing rain_flag reader. Recommend, then take to the counterpart.
q7.finding: DECISION RULED (self-adjudicated; see human_answer) -- ADD alongside, do not replace. GripEstimateRecord.rain_flag stays a non-Optional bool (it has live readers: error_record grip_store.py:202, tests/unit/physics/layer2/test_grip_store.py:100-101, test_grip_batch.py:28/42, test_class_utilization_observable.py:223) and is redefined as severity != dry; the graded fields arrive as NEW nullable columns that _migrate_missing_columns already knows how to ALTER-ADD. Grounds: the store's migration contract is explicitly additive-only ('Never drops or renames', grip_store.py:130-131), so removing a column would break every existing grip DB for no gain.

q8.title: [DECISION] Does the flat RAIN_SIGMA_INFLATION=4.0 become graded in severity, or stay flat with only the SELECTION criterion loosened?
q8.imperative: The issue asks only about exclusion, but a flat 4x on a zero-wet-lap session is the same over-aggression in sigma form. Recommend, then take to the counterpart.
q8.finding: DECISION RULED (self-adjudicated; see human_answer) -- GRADE the sigma inflation, preserving the conservative ceiling. RAIN_SIGMA_INFLATION=4.0 stays the value at full-wet and the factor interpolates down to 1.0 at fully-dry. Grounds: a flat 4x on a session with ZERO wet laps is the identical over-aggression the issue is about, just expressed in sigma rather than selection -- and recovering coverage is self-defeating if every recovered session arrives carrying a 4x penalty that makes a precision-weighted pool ignore it anyway. Keeping 4.0 as the ceiling means the genuinely-wet end of the behaviour is unchanged, so this cannot make anything less conservative than today. FLAGGED: this is the ruling I would most want the owner's word on, because it changes stored sigmas that #664-class consumers read, and it is a scope extension beyond the issue's literal text.

q9.title: [DECISION] Does issue 688 own the data-layer coverage extension (populating wet_lap_fraction for non-race sessions), or is that a separate issue?
q9.imperative: The grip fit runs over every session type but the wet-fraction seam is populated for races only. Without the extension the loosened rule has no signal to read for Q/SQ/S/FP. Recommend, then take to the counterpart.
q9.finding: DECISION RULED (self-adjudicated; see human_answer) -- YES, this issue owns the data-layer coverage extension. populate_wet_features_for_db must stop iterating races only (weather_features.py:224 get_sessions(session_type='R')) and cover every session type. Grounds: q2 measured ZERO non-race wet_lap_fraction rows in every season 2022-2025, while the grip fit runs over every type in SESSION_TYPES (grip_batch.py:65). Shipping a loosened threshold with no signal behind it for Q/SQ/S/FP would be a no-op dressed as a fix -- and thin/missing Q is precisely the coverage the #678 spike named as the crux.

q10.title: [DECISION] Where does the usable-for-pooling SELECTION predicate live so consumers stop reinventing it per-spike?
q10.imperative: The 20-of-36 drop happened in a consumer, not the producer. Decide whether this issue ships a named production predicate or only the graded severity field. Recommend, then take to the counterpart.
q10.finding: DECISION RULED (self-adjudicated; see human_answer) -- ship a NAMED PRODUCTION PREDICATE, in minimal form. One documented selection helper beside get_grip_at in grip_store.py plus a severity filter argument on GripStore.load, and nothing more -- no policy framework, no config surface. Grounds: the entire defect surfaced because the selection rule lived in a throwaway consumer where nobody could review it; leaving it there guarantees the next spike reinvents the any-wet rule. Bounding it to one function plus one filter argument keeps the change inside the issue's coverage-lever scope.

q11.title: [fact] What regeneration or re-batch does the change imply, and what does it cost?
q11.imperative: Determine whether the grip store must be re-run with --force, whether the season DBs need a wet-feature repopulate, and how expensive each is.
q11.finding: FACT RESOLVED -- two regenerations, both bounded, and they must be planned as gates rather than assumed. (i) Season DBs: populate_wet_features_for_db is DB-only, idempotent, network-free (weather_features.py:210-231); extending it past session_type='R' and re-running 2018-2026 is cheap -- it counts lap_times compounds for ~170 sessions per season. (ii) Grip store: GripStore._migrate_missing_columns (grip_store.py:123-135) is additive ALTER-ADD, so new columns self-heal to NULL on an existing grip DB; but the graded values only populate on a re-fit, so run_grip_batch(..., force=True) is required, which re-runs scipy curve_fit per session -- the same cost as #663's original build. Not multi-hour-class, but it is a real gate with its own evidence, not a footnote.

q12.title: [fact] What guards the conservative direction -- what evidence proves genuinely wet running is still excluded?
q12.imperative: Identify the known-wet sessions in 2022-2024 that any accepted rule MUST still exclude, and the known-dry-despite-a-shower sessions it MUST recover. These become frozen test cases.
q12.finding: FACT RESOLVED -- the frozen test corpus falls straight out of probe_rain.py. MUST STILL EXCLUDE (genuinely wet timed running, wet-lap fraction >= 0.6): 2022 Japan R 1.000, 2022 GreatBritain Q 1.000, 2022 Canada Q 0.993, 2023 Belgium S 1.000, 2024 Belgium Q 1.000, 2023 Canada Q 0.848, 2023 Netherlands Q 0.843, 2023 Austria S 0.840, 2023 Belgium SQ 0.766, 2024 Canada R 0.665, 2023 Belgium Q 0.622, 2022 Singapore R 0.622. MUST RECOVER (any-wet-sample flags them today; ZERO wet laps): 2022 Miami R, 2022 GreatBritain R, 2022 Hungary R, 2023 Australia Q, 2023 Azerbaijan S, 2023 Spain Q, 2023 Austria R, 2023 Brazil S/Q/R, 2024 Australia Q, 2024 Canada Q, 2024 Spain R, 2024 Austria R, 2024 Hungary Q, 2024 Brazil S. BORDERLINE (the band where the drying-track guard earns its keep): 2022 Monaco R 0.338, 2022 Brazil Q 0.334, 2022 EmiliaRomagna Q 0.293, 2023 Monaco R 0.293, 2023 Netherlands R 0.244, 2024 GreatBritain R 0.244, 2024 GreatBritain Q 0.231, and 2023 GreatBritain Q 0.013 (5 wet laps of 386 -- a genuine near-miss a 0.05 threshold correctly keeps).
